title: Cohomology and tensor invariance on a finite scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal G$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $H^q(T,\mathcal G)=0$ and $H^q(T,\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal L)=0$ for every $q>0$ (cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology], tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), both $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ and $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)$ are finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, and $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$. Consequently, the Euler characteristics of [def-pc-euler-characteristic] are defined and satisfy $\chi(T,\mathcal G)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ and $\chi(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\chi(T,\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), parts (3), (4), and (5) with the locally free sheaf of rank one $\mathcal L$

proof.text: *$T$ is finite, discrete and Noetherian.* The field $k$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is its maximal ideal $0$, and $A$ is a finite $k$-algebra: a finite $k$-basis of $A$ generates $A$ as a $k$-module [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] (with $R=k$, $B=A$), $A$ has finitely many prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$, all maximal, and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a finite discrete space [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: $T=\{t_1,\dots,t_r\}$ with $t_j=\mathfrak q_j$, and every singleton $\{t_j\}$ is open. Moreover $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal of $A$ is a $k$-subspace, so in a strictly increasing chain of ideals the dimensions strictly increase and are bounded by $\dim_kA$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Hence $T$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] (it is covered by the single affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian).

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof: 'In fact, by Lemma 04MG (varieties-lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0) the scheme Z is a finite disjoint union of spectra of local Artinian rings'

proof.text: *$\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ is finite-dimensional.* Since $T$ is locally Noetherian (Step 1), the coherent module $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) to the affine open $U=T$, whose ring of sections is $\mathcal O_T(T)=A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. As $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-module (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra] (with $R=k$, $B=A$, $M=\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$) shows that $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ is a finitely generated $k$-module, i.e. a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], so $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ is defined [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof: 'G is a coherent O_Z-module ... Z is affine'

proof.text: *$\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_T$.* By [def-sc-invertible-module], each point $t_j$ has an open neighbourhood $U_j$ with an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U_j}$-modules $\mathcal L|_{U_j}\cong\mathcal O_{U_j}$; restricting it to the open subset $\{t_j\}\subseteq U_j$ (Step 1) gives an isomorphism $\varphi_j:\mathcal L|_{\{t_j\}}\to\mathcal O_T|_{\{t_j\}}$. The opens $\{t_1\},\dots,\{t_r\}$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $T$. For an open $V\subseteq T$ the opens $V_j:=V\cap\{t_j\}$ cover $V$ with empty pairwise intersections, so the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal L$ and for $\mathcal O_T$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] says that restriction gives bijections $\mathcal L(V)\to\prod_j\mathcal L(V_j)$ and $\mathcal O_T(V)\to\prod_j\mathcal O_T(V_j)$ (the gluing condition on the overlaps is empty). Define $\varphi_V:\mathcal L(V)\to\mathcal O_T(V)$ as the map corresponding to $\prod_j(\varphi_j)_{V_j}$. It is $\mathcal O_T(V)$-linear and commutes with restriction to $V'\subseteq V$ because each $\varphi_j$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_{\{t_j\}}$-modules; the same construction applied to the inverses $\varphi_j^{-1}$ gives an inverse of $\varphi$. So $\varphi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal O_T$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules. (This is the source's 'since Z has dimension 0 the locally free sheaf $i^*\mathcal E$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus n}$', for $n=1$.)

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof: 'Since Z has dimension 0 the locally free sheaf i^*E is isomorphic to O_Z^{\oplus n}'

proof.text: *$\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L\cong\mathcal G$.* By functoriality of the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}\otimes\varphi$ (Step 3) is an isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal L\cong\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal O_T$. On each open $V$ the presheaf tensor product has sections $\mathcal G(V)\otimes_{\mathcal O_T(V)}\mathcal O_T(V)$, and $g\otimes a\mapsto ag$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathcal G(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], compatible with restrictions; so the presheaf tensor product is isomorphic to the sheaf $\mathcal G$, and its sheafification $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}\mathcal O_T$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal G$. Hence there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules $\psi:\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L\cong\mathcal G$. In particular $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent] (the conditions there are invariant under isomorphism), $\Gamma(T,\psi)$ is an $A$-linear, hence $k$-linear, isomorphism $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)\cong\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$, so by Step 2 $\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)$ is finite-dimensional with $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$, and since $H^q(T,-)$ is a functor [pqf-def-cohomology], $H^q(T,\psi)$ is an isomorphism $H^q(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)\cong H^q(T,\mathcal G)$ of $A$-modules for every $q\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof: 'i_*(G \otimes i^*E) = F \otimes E ... arguing as above we see that (5) holds'

proof.text: *Vanishing.* $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine and $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent (Step 2), so $H^q(T,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $q>0$ by [lem-pc-affine-vanishing]. By the isomorphisms $H^q(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)\cong H^q(T,\mathcal G)$ of Step 4, also $H^q(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=0$ for all $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite), proof: 'Since the dimension of Z is 0, we see Z is affine ... the higher cohomology groups of G are zero (Lemma 01XB)'

proof.text: *Euler characteristics.* The structure morphism $f:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine with the single nonempty open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ itself, its preimage $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine (so $f$ is affine), and $k\to A$ is finite (Step 1). Hence $f$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so $T$ is a proper $k$-scheme and, $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L$ being coherent (Step 4), [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] shows that $\chi(T,\mathcal G)=\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\dim_kH^i(T,\mathcal G)$ and $\chi(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\dim_kH^i(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)$ of [def-pc-euler-characteristic] are well-defined integers. By Step 5 only $i=0$ contributes, and $H^0(T,-)=\Gamma(T,-)$ (the $0$-th right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Gamma(T,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]), so $\chi(T,\mathcal G)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$ and $\chi(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)$, which are equal by Step 4. Thus $\chi(T,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\chi(T,\mathcal G)=\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal G)$.
